clue.text: Match extinguished, perhaps, in front of grate? Be clear

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming in front of means these pieces precede the last one

parts.note: to match something, as a colour does, is to go with it
a fire or light that is extinguished is out
to grate is to say something in a harsh, rasping voice, so grating is saying

explanation.surface: Someone lights a fire, the match goes out in front of the grate, and they are told to stand back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' just softens the surface. The definition is a verb phrase: something that goes without saying is clear to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact that goes without saying is too obvious to need stating, which is to be plainly evident.

clue.text: Crack and dent the result of crash

parts.note: crack as an adjective means first-rate or great (a crack shot)
a dent is a hollow or depression in a surface

explanation.surface: A car's damage report: a crack and a dent left after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's car crash is really the Wall Street Crash of 1929, which led into the 1930s slump.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1929 stock market crash is generally seen as the trigger of the worldwide economic slump that followed.

clue.text: Factory functions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as a noun is an industrial plant
second meaning: as a verb, ... means operates or functions properly

explanation.walkthrough: One word read first as a noun for a plant, then as a verb for operating.
explanation.definitionFit: A works is an industrial site such as a steelworks, and a machine that works operates as intended.

clue.text: Think idly about doll maybe joker's given to husband

indicators.note: given to means the next piece is added on after

parts.note: a doll is an example of a toy
a wit is a joker, someone clever and funny

explanation.surface: A wife muses idly while a doll and a jester figure are handed to her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with an idea is to consider it casually, without serious intent.

clue.text: Mostly nice room tidied up for Greek character

indicators.note: tidying a room rearranges its contents, so these letters are put in a new order
mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: the word with its last letter cut
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pleasant room is put in order for a Greek visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims nice to NIC; mixing NIC with ROOM gives the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, the short O.

clue.text: Young child is losing love for one small fish

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, and one is the Roman numeral I, so O is swapped for I

parts.note: a toddler is a young child just learning to walk

explanation.surface: A toddler gives up his love for one small fish, perhaps a pet goldfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping O for I in TODDLER gives the answer; 'love' is O as a tennis score and 'one' is I.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddler is a minnow or stickleback, any tiny fish, and by extension a small child.

clue.text: Nimby is one jumping on my car

indicators.note: jumping letters leap about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A local objector leaps onto the speaker's car in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nimby' looks like the protester in the scene; it is the example that defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: NIMBY is formed from the initials of 'not in my back yard', so it is a word made of initial letters.

clue.text: Rash old American supporting the compiler's favourite university

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below the pieces before it

parts.note: the setter's means I am, written IM
a pet is a favourite (teacher's pet)

explanation.surface: An elderly American gives backing to the setter's favourite college, perhaps unwisely.
explanation.walkthrough: Order matters: 'old American' comes last because 'supporting' sets it under the rest in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetuous behaviour is impulsive and hasty, done without thinking, just as rash behaviour is.

clue.text: Excited girls tour cheese region

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Thrilled young women go on a tour of cheesemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: The cheese is apt: Double Gloucester comes from this English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloucestershire is an English county in the south-west, home of the Cotswolds and Double Gloucester cheese.

clue.text: One proverbially arriving in good time — for vermicelli?

definitions.text: One proverbially arriving in good time — for vermicelli?

parts.words: One proverbially arriving in good time — for vermicelli?
parts.note: the proverb says the first one up catches the worm, and vermicelli is Italian for little worms

explanation.walkthrough: Vermicelli means 'little worms' in Italian, so the punctual proverbial creature arrives early for its worms.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a person who rises or arrives before others, from the saying about catching the worm.

clue.text: Substitute furniture men brought back behind theatre

indicators.note: behind means the reversed piece comes after the theatre

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

indicators.note: brought back means the letters are reversed

parts.note: OR (other ranks) means soldiers who are not officers, the men

explanation.surface: Removal men bring a replacement sofa round the back of the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Repro is short for reproduction, furniture made to imitate an antique style in place of the original.

clue.text: Short session drinking wine, fuller-flavoured

indicators.note: drinking means taking the wine inside
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a term is an academic session
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A brief drinking session with wine that has more flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastier means having more flavour, which is exactly a comparative of fuller-flavoured.

clue.text: Every one getting 50 per cent off, Lucy nabs ticket for loco

indicators.text: Every one getting 50 per cent off
indicators.note: each of the three words loses its second half, keeping just the front

parts.note: first half kept
first half kept
first half kept

explanation.surface: Everyone gets half-price, and Lucy grabs a ticket for the train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' looks like a locomotive in this railway scene; it is the American slang word for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is informal Spanish-derived slang for crazy, so a lunatic is a loco person.

clue.text: Love of French poet's work

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A French poet writes about love.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, often addressed to a subject, so it is a typical piece by a poet.

clue.text: Like some old crocks, fear the new to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Old crocks, decrepit old folk, are wary of anything new.
explanation.walkthrough: An old crock is usually a worn-out person or car; here it is a crock, a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocks are clay pots, and earthenware vessels are made of baked clay.

clue.text: Search victim for gun part

parts.note: to rifle is to search through hurriedly, as a thief does
a butt is the target or victim of a joke

explanation.surface: A robber searches a victim for a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The rifle butt is the shoulder end of the stock of a long gun.

clue.text: Mutton producer solver mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken aloud, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: the solver is you, the person reading the clue

explanation.surface: The solver is told they have been named as a mutton producer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutton is the meat of a mature sheep, and a female sheep is what produces it.

clue.text: Staff succeeded, on strike for cleaners

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the next piece

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard
a rod is a staff or stick
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Office staff, having won their claim, stay on strike over the cleaners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' and 'strike' suggest an industrial dispute; they are a rod and a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramrod pushes the charge into a muzzle-loading gun and is also used to clean the barrel.

clue.text: Opener for Arsenal — on top of game since

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of means placed above the next piece
the opener of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter used
Go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A football report: Arsenal's opening goal put them on top of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago and since both mean in the past before now: three years ago, or three years since.

clue.text: Pure breed regularly okay with daughter

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

parts.note: second and fourth letters
fine means okay

explanation.surface: A pure-bred animal, fine as a bloodline, passed to a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined sugar or oil has been processed to remove impurities, so it is pure.

clue.text: Cheat, turning up with Oscar? I'm unable to carry that off!

definitions.text: I'm unable to carry that off!

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a con is a cheat or swindle
and means with
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone asked to pull off a swindle with an Oscar statuette refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal pidgin-style refusal meaning it cannot be managed.

clue.text: Hat the wrong way around, Miss Woodhouse's predicament?

indicators.note: the wrong way around means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's Emma

explanation.surface: Austen's heroine has a fashion crisis, her hat on back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult situation with no good choice, a predicament or quandary.

clue.text: King's heading south-east to visit coastal town for brief inspection

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so these letters are put inside the town

parts.note: Looe is a fishing town on the Cornish coast

indicators.note: heading here means followed by a direction, so the next piece comes after

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: The monarch heads south-east to call on a seaside town for a quick look round.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOE is a small coastal town in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is an informal quick look or once-over, a short inspection.

clue.text: Sheds wiry character erected right away

parts.note: a wiry person is lean

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means stood upright, so read from the bottom
right away means R, for right, is removed

parts.note: a sort is a character (a good sort)

explanation.surface: A thin figure puts up sheds immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once'; it removes R from SORT, leaving SOT, which 'erected' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed built against a wall, with a roof sloping one way.

clue.text: Former nun is retiring, becoming pensioner?

parts.note: former means old, as in an old boss

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: a nun is a sister
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ex-nun is retiring, becoming a pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking IS out of SISTER leaves STER. The question mark marks that not every pensioner is an oldster, or vice versa.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an elderly person, the kind likely to draw a state pension.

clue.text: Desperate to avoid Germany's rage

indicators.note: to avoid means this letter is left out

parts.note: dire means desperate, as in dire straits
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A desperate attempt to avoid German anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for anger, so it means rage.

clue.text: Redesigned client's pattern

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A designer reworks a customer's pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out template used to paint a design, so it serves as a pattern.

clue.text: Runs away with sailors across the Channel

indicators.note: across means the sailors span round the other piece

parts.note: ABs, able seamen, are sailors
a duct is a channel or conduit

explanation.surface: Smugglers or kidnappers escape with sailors over the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Channel' sounds like the sea between England and France; it is a duct.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct someone is to take them away by force, which is to run off with them.

clue.text: Dog's firm resistance when going over grit occasionally

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
R is the physics symbol for resistance

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter

parts.note: first and third letters

explanation.surface: A dog stubbornly resists being walked over gritted paths.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small Welsh herding dog, famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Lay to rest in ancient city before noon

indicators.note: before means these come ahead of the next piece

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A burial in an ancient city before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: To inurn is to place ashes in an urn, and hence to bury or entomb.

clue.text: Bones of setter so long with painful stress injury

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
ta-ta is an informal goodbye, like so long
RSI is repetitive strain injury

explanation.surface: The compiler's bones are suffering a painful strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' is the compiler, not a dog, and ta-ta is a British informal goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: The metatarsals are the five long bones of the foot between ankle and toes.

clue.text: Conscription: several in action at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Several conscripts see action in a naval battle.
explanation.definitionFit: National service was compulsory military service for young British men until 1960, a form of the draft.
